description: Acceptance suite for the /build dispatcher rebuild. Pre-registered BEFORE any skill content was written. Paths are relative to the repo root of the worktree.
runner_note: runner=shell cases are executed by evals/run_checks.py (deterministic, no LLM). runner=llm-judge cases require ANTHROPIC_API_KEY; if absent they are reported JUDGE-PENDING and never silently passed. runner=manual-benchmark cases require an end-to-end agent run and are reported RUN-PENDING until executed.

cases.description: The routing table must name 100% of the practice skills actually installed in this environment (inventory frozen in GOLD.md). Zero missing, and every entry must carry a skip rule.
SKILL.md itself (not only references/) must carry the explicit phase -> skill -> skip routing table, because dispatch decisions happen at the top level.
Valid YAML frontmatter with name+description; SKILL.md under 300 lines (progressive disclosure).
Every references/ and scripts/ path mentioned in SKILL.md must exist on disk, and every file in references/ must be linked from SKILL.md (no dead links, no orphans).
test-driven-development must be routed as non-skippable: its routing-table entry must say it is never skipped, and SKILL.md must state the no-production-code-without-a-failing-test law.

The skill must mandate that every build run writes ACCEPTANCE.md + evals/cases.json (in the /eval skill's format) and commits them BEFORE any implementation code, and must point at the /eval skill for the format.
The skill must document a loop driver that re-runs acceptance until green: the /loop pattern, a runtime-independent shell fallback, a bounded max-iteration cap, and stuck detection.
Running the bundled init script in a scratch dir must emit BOTH the ACCEPTANCE artifact and an executable loop driver, plus a cases.json skeleton. Mechanical proof of the integral requirement.
The generated acceptance checker must actually fail when acceptance is unmet and pass once met. A driver that always exits 0 is worthless.
All five CRITICAL safety-review items from the reference copy survive the rebuild (SQL/data, LLM trust boundary, auth, secret exposure, injection) and are wired to a blocking gate.
Every WORKFLOW_GATE invocation must be guarded so it no-ops when the hook script is absent (restricted sandbox). No unguarded invocation anywhere in the skill tree.
No credential-shaped literals anywhere in the skill tree, and an explicit no-secrets rule for generated code.
Two runtimes: a capability matrix for local Claude Code vs restricted sandbox must exist, and every MCP- or plugin-dependent step must be marked optional/guarded. No step may hard-require an MCP.
Bundled shell scripts must pass `bash -n` and contain no hardcoded absolute user paths that would break in the restricted sandbox.
Three benchmark project specs exist: a CLI tool, an API endpoint with tests, and a bugfix scenario. Each spec must declare its own acceptance criteria and expected artifact set.

The bugfix fixture must contain a REAL seeded bug: the fixture's own test suite passes (bug not trivially visible), the held-out verification test fails against shipped code, and applying the known one-line fix makes it pass.
End-to-end: run /build against 01-cli-tool.md. Must emit ACCEPTANCE.md and a loop driver BEFORE the first implementation commit, and end with all acceptance checks green.
End-to-end: run /build against 02-api-endpoint.md. Tests must be committed before the handler (TDD spine), and the acceptance artifact + loop driver must be emitted.

End-to-end: run /build against 03-bugfix.md on the seeded-bug fixture. systematic-debugging must be routed before any fix, a failing repro test must exist before the fix commit, and the held-out verification test must pass afterwards.
Code produced by the three benchmark runs is graded by an LLM judge (different model family from the builder) against the code-quality rubric. Mean >= 4.0/5 with no single benchmark below 3.5.

expected.rubric: Score 1-5 on each dimension: (1) Correctness - does it do what the spec says, with edge cases handled? (2) Test quality - do tests pin real behaviour, or are they tautological? (3) Simplicity - is anything present that is not load-bearing? (4) Readability - could a new engineer follow it in one pass? (5) Safety - input handling, error surfacing, no secrets, no silent failure. Report per-dimension scores and an overall mean.

cases.description: An LLM judge reads SKILL.md cold and must be able to state, for a given task type, which practice skill fires at each phase and which are skipped.

expected.rubric: Score 1-5: (1) Given 'fix a flaky test', can the judge name the exact routing path from SKILL.md alone? (2) Are skip conditions unambiguous rather than 'use judgement'? (3) Is the acceptance-first + loop-driver requirement stated as mandatory and unmissable? (4) Is it clear what degrades in the restricted sandbox? (5) Is SKILL.md free of content that belongs in references/?
